description: The time column. Its presence makes the table a time-series table.
name: time-column

description: Comma-separated columns that identify a series.
name: series-key

description: Partition size: how much time one partition covers.
name: chunk-interval

default.derived: true with a series key, else false

description: Rows with the same (series, time) count once; the latest write wins. Applied within an append, by the Timelake reader, and by compaction. Fixed at creation: files written with it off may hold copies, which the reader would then miss.
name: dedup

description: The column holding each row's insertion time (`ingest_time=False` or `--no-ingest-time` leaves it out). Each append fills it with the time the append started, unless the input brings its own values. Among rows with the same (series, time), the latest insertion wins, then the later commit.
name: ingest-time-column

description: Maintenance drops partitions that end before now minus this duration, e.g. 90d.
name: retention

description: Run size-tiered compaction, retention, and snapshot expiry inline after appends. One append can override it (`maintain=` in Python, `--no-maintain` on the CLI).
name: auto-maintain

description: Inline compaction merges a size tier of a partition once it has this many files.
name: compact-min-files

description: Inline maintenance rewrites a partition whole (sorted, duplicates removed) once the table holds data newer than the partition's end by this much and the partition has two small files, whether the append touched it or not. `off` leaves it to the size tiers.
name: compact-cold-after

description: The Timelake reader returns only the latest write of each (series, time), before compaction has removed the older copies. Has no effect on tables with dedup off.
name: read-dedup

description: How the reader removes copies: `merge` merges the files that may share keys in key order; `keys-first` lists the older copies from the key columns, then reads the files like any scan and leaves them out (slower on the industrial IoT benchmark).
name: read-dedup-strategy

description: The Timelake reader applies filters while decoding Parquet pages, cheapest first, and decodes the other columns only for the rows that pass. Less decoding when filters keep few rows, but each row group's filter columns and other columns are fetched one after the other. `auto` is on for local files and off on object storage, where first queries wait for the extra round trip; `true` suits repeat queries served from the cache.
name: filter-pushdown

description: How `time_weighted_mean` gets each series' readings in time order. It sums runs of readings in order and joins them; runs that overlap in time can't be joined. `segments`: as the files come (an overlap is an error). `merge`: files that overlap on the series and time, or aren't sorted, are merged in order first (as dedup on read does). `auto`: `merge` for tables with dedup off and such files, else `segments`.
name: time-weighted-mean

description: A query sorted by the time column, newest first, with a limit (`ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT k`) reads the newest time partition first and older ones only while they can still hold one of the k newest rows.
name: newest-first

description: The Timelake reader skips row groups and pages whose range of a column holds none of the values of a `column IN (…)` filter with more than 20 values, which DataFusion doesn't prune with: lists in the query, and, on scans that don't filter rows while decoding (object storage by default), the key lists of a join's runtime filter.
name: in-list-pruning

description: Size at which compaction output and writes roll to a new file (256 MiB).
name: target-file-size-bytes

description: Parquet row group size. Page indexes keep single-series reads selective inside large row groups.
name: row-group-rows

description: Expire snapshots older than this, keeping at least `min-snapshots` and at most `max-snapshots`.
name: snapshot-retention

description: Snapshots always kept, whatever their age.
name: min-snapshots

description: Snapshots kept at most: older ones expire even if younger than `snapshot-retention`.
name: max-snapshots

description: Format of the head object (`metadata/timelake-head`): `arrow`, `json`, a registered codec, or `none` for no head.
name: head-format

description: Room in the head for the last-value index, then the Parquet footers of the newest files (1 MiB). What doesn't fit is read separately.
name: head-inline-bytes

description: No snapshot expires before this time. `timelake upgrade` sets it so the upgrade can be rolled back.
name: keep-snapshots-until

description: The Timelake reader answers a `GROUP BY time_bucket(…)` query on this table from a rollup that matches it. Buckets changed since the rollup's last refresh, and partial buckets at the edges of the time range, still come from this table, so the answer is the same either way.
name: rollup-routing

description: On a rollup: inline maintenance after an append to its raw table refreshes it once its last refresh is this old. `off` leaves it to `timelake maintain` and `REFRESH MATERIALIZED ROLLUP`.
name: rollup-refresh-interval

description: Rows per Parquet data page in the files written. Smaller pages make compaction from a Worker use less memory (it holds a page per column of each file it merges: 8,192 rows peaked at 77 MiB merging 24 TSBS files, 20,000 at 123 MiB) and page pruning finer, at a few percent more bytes (TSBS: +3.6%) and slower scans below about 8,000 rows.
name: data-page-rows

description: The Timelake reader uses a table version it loaded or checked this long before checking for a newer one, so queries in that time send no request for it and can miss commits by other processes. `0s` checks on every query. This process's own commits are seen at once, and writers always check.
name: version-check-interval

description: On a raw table: its rollups, comma-separated. `CREATE` and `DROP MATERIALIZED ROLLUP` keep it.
name: rollups

description: On a rollup: the raw table it summarises.
name: rollup-source

description: On a rollup: the width of its time buckets.
name: rollup-bucket

description: On a rollup: its aggregates, each an output column, a function, and the column it reads.
name: rollup-aggregates

default.derived: the current format for new tables; 0.1.0 if absent

description: The table format. Timelake refuses tables of a newer format it can't handle; `timelake upgrade` brings a table to the current format.
name: format-version
